summary: Iteration 13 — frontend-only verification of the two Guide enhancements: (1) TVFocusGuideView-based FocusGuide wrapper around the guide grid and (2) A-Z fast-scroll rail on both Timeline and Box grids. Tested on the web preview (https://iptv-player-guide.preview.emergentagent.com) at mobile viewport 390x844. RESULTS — ALL 8 REVIEW-REQUEST ITEMS PASS. (1) Guide loads without crashing in timeline mode by default: [data-testid='epg-timeline-grid'] rendered and 688 channels populated within ~2s. (2) A-Z rail [data-testid='az-rail'] visible on the right of the guide. Tapping az-S scrolled the list from '5 Starmax / A&E' (top region) to 'Science Channel / Screen Pix' region — visible channel set changed cleanly. Tapping az-B also scrolled the list (5 Starmax → Animal Planet WEST/Aspire/AXS TV region — first B channel just below). (3) Rail correctly hides letters with no channels: absent letters detected = ['az-J','az-K','az-Q','az-X','az-Z'] and 22 letters (#,A-I,L-P,R-W,Y) are rendered — matching the actual data set. (4) mode-box-btn switches to Box grid: [data-testid='epg-box-grid'] visible AND [data-testid='az-rail'] still visible in Box mode; az-S tap in Box mode also scrolled visible cards from '5 Starmax' to 'Reelz Channel/Science Channel/Screen Pix' region. (5) mode-timeline-btn returns to timeline grid: [data-testid='epg-timeline-grid'] re-rendered and AZ rail still functions. (6) Group chips (chip-All, chip-Favorites, chip-Local, chip-Movies, chip-Sports, chip-TV) all filter correctly: chip-Favorites yields 0 channel rows (no favorites set), chip-All yields 70 channel row nodes in the viewport buffer. (7) guide-refresh-btn works — click triggers refresh without crash, no red screen. (8) Tabs regression check: Favorites, Search, Settings tabs all navigate cleanly (urls /favorites, /search, /settings) and render without errors; TV Guide tab returns to the guide. CONSOLE — 0 uncaught JS errors across the entire flow. FocusGuide wrapper correctly falls back to plain View on web (RN.TVFocusGuideView is undefined on react-native-web) — no runtime issue in web preview. Native-only D-pad focus-trap behavior is out of scope per the review-request note (only exercisable in an Android TV native build). MINOR UX OBSERVATION (non-blocking): FlashList.scrollToIndex used by AZRail does not place the target letter's row precisely at the top of the viewport — a few rows of the previous letter remain visible above (e.g. after az-S, 3 XAZRLZ 'Reelz Channel' rows sit above 'Science Channel' at top=213). This is FlashList default viewPosition behavior; passing viewPosition:0 (or a small offset) to scrollToIndex would pin the target row exactly at the top for a cleaner UX. Not a functional bug — list clearly scrolls and target letter's channels are on-screen. Deprecated packages / RN-specific issues detected: same carryover pointerEvents='none' -> style deprecation warning on TimelineGrid nowLine (cosmetic web-only, unrelated to this iteration).

issues: FlashList.scrollToIndex(i, {animated:true}) leaves a few rows of the previous letter visible above the target row. Consider passing viewPosition:0 (and viewOffset if there is a sticky header) so the tapped letter's first channel is pinned to the exact top of the viewport. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/TimelineGrid.tsx:183 and /app/frontend/src/components/BoxGrid.tsx:105 — both call scrollToIndex without a viewPosition.

react_native_issues.issue: Cosmetic web-only warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Still present on TimelineGrid nowLine. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/TimelineGrid.tsx:255 (styles.nowLine uses pointerEvents:'none' inside StyleSheet — actually already migrated to style). If any remaining prop usage exists, it is carryover from prior iterations, not this iteration's change.

action_items: OPTIONAL UX polish: pass viewPosition:0 to FlashList.scrollToIndex in AZRail callbacks so the tapped letter's first channel is pinned to the very top of the viewport (currently a couple of rows of the previous letter remain visible above). Refs: TimelineGrid.tsx:183, BoxGrid.tsx:105.
NONE required for correctness — all 8 review-request items pass on web. Native-only D-pad focus-trap behavior must be validated on an actual Android TV build (out of scope for web preview).
critical_code_review_comments: FocusGuide (TVFocusGuideView.tsx) — clean runtime resolution: const Native = RN.TVFocusGuideView; falls back to a plain View when Native is undefined. Web-safe (react-native-web has no TVFocusGuideView). trapFocus* props are destructured before spread so they don't leak onto the DOM. GOOD.

AZRail — sensibly hides itself when < 3 letters have channels (active.length<3 return null), uses Haptics.selectionAsync() before onSelect, and hitSlop:4 improves touch target on the tiny (22x20) letter cells. testIDs 'az-rail' and 'az-<L>' present.

AZRail 22x20 letter cells are BELOW the recommended 44x44 minimum touch target — acceptable for a rail (users can slide vertically) but individual letter taps on a phone may misfire; consider bumping to 28x28 with negative margins.
TimelineGrid / BoxGrid — both now hold a FlashList ref and forward the index to scrollToIndex inside a try/catch. Good defensive coding.

FocusGuide wraps the grid in index.tsx (line 134). Since FocusGuide falls back to plain View on web, the AZRail (position:'absolute', right:2) is correctly positioned relative to the grid area. Verified visually — rail sits on the right edge, unaffected by the header/chip row.
The rail is rendered INSIDE both TimelineGrid.body and BoxGrid.wrap — correct scoping so it moves with the grid area, not the header.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Base URL: https://iptv-player-guide.preview.emergentagent.com. Mobile viewport 390x844. Guide screen: [data-testid='epg-timeline-grid'] and [data-testid='epg-box-grid'] both host an [data-testid='az-rail'] on the right. Rail children are testID 'az-#' + 'az-<LETTER>' — only letters with matching channels are rendered. In this dataset the visible letters were: #, A-I, L-P, R-W, Y (J, K, Q, X, Z were absent, correctly hidden). FlashList's testIDs include buffer duplicates suffixed with '#<n>' — filter them out with `if '#' not in tid`. To verify a scroll change, capture visible epg-channel-* nodes by getBoundingClientRect() top<800 and compare first 3 before/after tap. Note: scrollToIndex without viewPosition doesn't pin to the exact top; a couple of previous-letter rows remain above the target. Native TVFocusGuideView, D-pad trap, and player route are out of scope for web preview.
rca_of_issue: No functional issues — the FocusGuide/AZRail additions are working as designed on web. FocusGuide correctly falls back to plain View when RN.TVFocusGuideView is undefined (react-native-web). AZRail correctly builds letter→first-index map, hides empty letters, and jumps FlashList via scrollToIndex. Only minor UX polish (viewPosition:0) suggested — not a bug.
